content:
Maya: Heads up — noticed console charts stutter + large main bundle after yesterday's runtime rollout. Delta looks like the bundle eviction pipeline got more aggressive and KV-prefetch fallback is causing synchronous re-fetch loops. Screenshot: https://img.gg/console-stall.png :eyes:
Sam: which canary and commit? can you grab a flame/profile?
Maya: Canary 3, commit d4c3f7a. Repro: open Dashboard -> pick 7d -> scroll / pan around. JS main thread spikes ~300-500ms and sparkline paints block.
Dmitri: Any related errors in CDN logs? are we seeing 200s or a bunch of 304/forced revalidate? :face_with_monocle:
Maya: Quick log sample (from the worker handling bundle fetches):
```
GET /assets/chunk-metrics.2f9c.js?v=2026-03-19 200 64ms
Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate
x-kv-hit: false
x-eviction-reason: size-pressure
x-route-id: eu-scoreboard
```
Maya: The pattern is: x-kv-hit false, immediate refetch from origin, then another miss — thrash.
Li: Did we flip prefetch priority for metric panels in that PR? I vaguely remember lowering prefetch to avoid prefetching huge chart chunks.
Sam: Yeah PR #4123 lowered prefetch priority and added aggressive eviction when worker mem > 2GB. The idea was to prevent huge memory spikes but looks like it caused churn for active dashboards.
Dmitri: Also note we changed routing policy last week to send certain requests to the low-cost pool (fallback) when primary is saturated. That pool doesn't share KV affinity so you get cold KV reads. Combined with eviction this explains the pattern.
Maya: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert the eviction threshold change on canary OR pin the 'metrics' chunk namespace to never-evict for the canary rollout. Also revert prefetch lowering for high-cardinality dashboards.
Sam: I can patch envs: set EVICTION_THRESHOLD=3GB (was 2GB) and PREFETCH_PRIORITY=normal on canary to validate. If that helps, we roll out to prod slowly.
Li: We should also add telemetry: record x-kv-hit and x-route-id in console bundle fetch metrics. Right now we only have token-level traces, not bundle-level miss-rate aggregated by route. I'll add counter console.kv_fetch.hit and console.kv_fetch.miss with labels {route_id,chunk_namespace}.
Dmitri: Good. Also add a short-lived canary guard that fires if bundle miss rate > 5% for 3m. Would have caught this before users hit it.
Maya: For debugging, here's a tiny repro script to hammer the dashboard load and collect header traces (run from EU):
```
for i in 1..100; do curl -I 'https://console.redwood.ai/assets/chunk-metrics.2f9c.js?v=2026-03-19' -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' | egrep -i 'x-kv-hit|x-eviction-reason|x-route-id'; sleep 0.2; done
```
Maya: Running it shows a ~40% miss rate pre-patch.
Sam: Deploying the env patch now to canary-3. Will report back in ~5m.
Deploy-bot: deploy started canary-redwood-console:canary-3 by sam (env patch). ETA ~5m.
Sam: Patch deployed. early signs: cpu jitter reduced and chart main-thread blocks dropped to ~80ms. still some misses but much better.
Dmitri: Please keep routing change in the checklist — we need to ensure route affinity stays with primary pool for KV-backed assets. I'll open a short PR to add a route-affinity flag on pool selection.
Li: Instrumentation note: I'll emit metrics within 1h and wire an alert dashboard for ops. Also will add a short trace span when we fall back to origin so we can correlate user impact.
Maya: Thanks. Action items: Sam revert/soften eviction on canary (done), Dmitri PR for route-affinity guard, Li add metrics + alert, Maya will draft a short postmortem + RFC for guardrails around eviction+routing coupling.
Sam: timeline for RFC?
Maya: I'll draft RFC today, aim for review tomorrow.
Dmitri: One more: add a tiny client-side backoff when bundle re-request frequency > 2/s so dashboards don't hotloop requests on poor networks. Could be a quick complement to server-side fixes.
Maya: Good call. I'll prototype an exponential jitter backoff wrapped around our asset loader.
Li: Monitoring alert when bundle miss rate spikes -> page experience degradation link to runbook.
Maya: Great. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sam: +1, thanks.
Dmitri: Filing tracking items now.
Maya: I'll follow up with the RFC link and screenshots in this thread.
